title: Tooling: explain every registered replay selection
body:
## Change and scope

Add `--explain-plan PATH` to `research_package.py --changed-since`. The sidecar reports every selected package's changed package files, declared inputs and shared replay controls, with exact base/head, working-manifest SHA256 and unmatched changed paths. Selection and explanations share one pass; the normal flat/batched matrix and GitHub outputs are unchanged.

This explains routing, not execution or mathematical acceptance. The planner retains its current working-tree inventory and sparse-checkout limits. Report creation is atomic and occurs before matrix publication; failed validation or report writing produces no new matrix.

## Task and overlap

Base `997e6a9ca7b4f95d50e366f61412fd640d72a88a`, refreshed before selection and publication. Verification-engineering session seed 87; explicit workflow simplification, related to the `portable-replay` card with scope changed to transparent dependency selection. [Claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200#discussioncomment-18991694).

PRs, issues and recent #1200/#1166 comments were refreshed. Exact JSON comparison was rejected as a candidate because PR2040 and its follow-ups already cover it. Searches found no same-scope selection-explanation claim. This preserves the earlier selector and invalidation fixes rather than redefining their coverage; no dependency on PR3138/3139.

## Validation

`python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_plan_explanations.py' -v`

Six real-Git tests pass under Python 3.14.7. They cover simultaneous reasons, exact unchanged stdout/batched matrices/GitHub fields, Unicode/newline paths, rename/deletion triggers, unrelated changes, all-tracked mode, invalid manifests, output failures and conflicting output paths. The current checkout's all-tracked explanation also agrees exactly with its selected matrix. Full Python 3.12 tool-suite results follow below.

## Credit and next questions

Tekalign, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0. Builds on Douglas Colkitt's registered package workflow and Charles Bethin's replay-selection/invalidation controls, retaining all predecessor attribution. See the package guide's explanation section. A complete committed-manifest inventory for sparse checkouts would require a separate coverage design; this PR explicitly does not claim to solve that question.

Python 3.12.14: **228 research-tool tests pass, 11 platform-specific skips**. The checkout smoke check covers 83,211 tracked paths and its 18 materialized registered manifests; it is not a claim of complete sparse-repository package coverage. No mathematical replays were launched locally. Hosted CI is separate.
